question: According to Ohm’s law:
solution:
The correct answer is __**V ∝ I at constant temperature.**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• According to **Ohm's law**, the relationship between **voltage (V), current (I), and resistance (R)** is given by V = IR.
 
• "V ∝ I at constant temperature" is a **correct** statement as per Ohm's law.
 
• It means that if the **temperature remains constant**, the voltage across a conductor is **directly proportional **to the current flowing through it.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Only when the given **temperature **and the other **physical parameters **stay constant does Ohm's law apply.
 
• In some components, the **temperature rises **when the **current is increased.**
 
• A l**ight bulb's filament **serves as an illustration of this, wherein increasing current causes the filament's temperature to rise.
 
• Ohm's law** cannot** be applied in this situation.
 
• The filament of the lightbulb **defies Ohm's Law**.
